18	/// Why a remote read or action failed.
19	///
20	/// Deliberately NOT folded into `VCSError`: that enum is the backend-*read* taxonomy
21	/// (`lockContention`/`staleSnapshot`/`partialData`/…) and `WorkroomStatusResolver.failure(for:)`
22	/// switches over it exhaustively to choose a sidebar badge. `.authRequired` has no sidebar badge and
23	/// no sensible answer there, so adding it would force a meaningless decision in a function that
24	/// currently has a principled one for every case. Same reasoning that put `CIResolution`/`PRResolution`
25	/// beside their resolver instead of in `VCSModels.swift`.
26	enum VCSRemoteFailure: Equatable, Sendable {
27	  /// `git`/`jj` not on PATH. Distinct from `VCSToolVersions`' floor check, which runs at launch —
28	  /// this is the same condition caught at the point of use.
29	  case toolMissing(String)
30	  case timedOut(VCSRemoteAction)
31	  /// Credentials were needed and none were available.
32	  case authRequired(String)
33	  /// The host's key isn't in `known_hosts`. `BatchMode=yes` turns what would be an interactive
34	  /// confirmation into this, so it needs its own copy — telling the user to configure a credential
35	  /// helper would be wrong advice.
36	  case hostKeyUnverified(String)
37	  case noRemote
38	  /// Push rejected (non-fast-forward). The engine NEVER force-pushes; the UI offers Pull.
39	  case rejected(String)
40	  /// git refused because tracked files would be overwritten.
41	  case dirtyWorkingTree(String)
42	  /// A failed or killed `git pull --rebase` left `rebase-merge`/`rebase-apply` behind. The repo needs
43	  /// `git rebase --abort`, so the UI must offer that instead of a retry that will fail identically.
44	  case rebaseInProgress
45	  /// A repo lock was held — git `index.lock`/`packed-refs.lock`, or jj's `git_import_export.lock`.
46	  ///
47	  /// The payload is the lock file itself when we could find it on disk, and that distinction decides
48	  /// what the UI offers. **`nil` ⇒ transient contention**, so Retry is genuine: another command held the
49	  /// lock briefly and by the next click it is likely gone. **Non-nil ⇒ a lock file is sitting there
50	  /// right now**, and retrying fails identically every time — the same reasoning that makes
51	  /// `rebaseInProgress` offer Abort instead of Retry.
52	  ///
53	  /// A leftover lock is what a SIGKILLed git leaves: the runner escalates to `killTree` two seconds
54	  /// after SIGTERM, and SIGKILL cannot be caught, so git's own cleanup never runs.
55	  ///
56	  /// Workroom does NOT delete it. Whether a lock is truly abandoned or held by a git running right now
57	  /// is not knowable from outside the process — `lsof` can't be trusted for it, and removing a live
58	  /// lock corrupts the index — so this reports and explains, and the removal stays the user's call.
59	  /// That is also what git's own message tells you to do.
60	  case locked(VCSLockFile?)
61	  /// jj refused to rewrite a commit protected by `immutable_heads()` — reached by Pull, whose
62	  /// `jj rebase -b @` moves the whole branch containing `@`, and that branch usually contains a
63	  /// remote-tracked commit. Measured on jj 0.43 for a workroom based off a feature branch while trunk
64	  /// moved on: `Error: Commit 4c8e754829da is immutable`.
65	  ///
66	  /// Offers no retry, for `rebaseInProgress`'s reason: the destination doesn't change between clicks, so
67	  /// every retry fails identically. The real fix is remembering each workroom's own base instead of
68	  /// guessing `trunk()` — filed, not built.
69	  case immutableHistory(String)
70	  /// jj refuses to push a commit with an empty description, changes or not. This is the state a workroom
71	  /// sits in the moment you edit a file and before you write a message, so it is the most reachable
72	  /// failure on the push path, not an edge case. Measured: `Error: Won't push commit 050e657d3c36 since
73	  /// it has no description`.
74	  case needsDescription(String)
75	  case other(String)
76	}

123	/// The seam for VCS operations that **write** — remote state reads plus fetch/push/pull.
124	///
125	/// Separate from `VCSProviding` on purpose. That protocol's doc calls it "the single seam the app
126	/// **reads** VCS data through", and four resolvers construct providers freely and call them with no
127	/// gate. Putting `fetch` there would mean nothing structurally prevented a read path from firing a
128	/// network mutation — the opposite of what `JJSnapshotGate` exists to guarantee. Keeping writes on
129	/// their own protocol also gives the injected `StatusCommandRunning` a home: `GitProvider` and
130	/// `RustJJProvider` are stateless value types constructed at four call sites with nowhere to put one.
131	///
132	/// This is the growth surface for the rest of the VCS write phase (commit/amend, bookmark management,
133	/// the deep jj ops), which is why it's a protocol with a factory rather than one standalone resolver —
134	/// otherwise each later operation re-derives repo kind and wires its own runner.
135	protocol VCSWriting: Sendable {
136	  /// Everything the toolbar renders, as ONE coherent snapshot.
137	  func remoteState(path: String, projectRoot: String) async -> VCSRemoteResolution
138	  func fetch(path: String, projectRoot: String, remote: String) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
139	  /// `anonymousRevision` is used only by jj, and only when `@` carries no bookmark: it is the revision
140	  /// the auto-created `push-<change-id>` bookmark will point at. Compute it with
141	  /// `CLIVCSWriter.jjPushRevision(hasChanges:hasDescription:)` — pushing a bare `@` fails when the
142	  /// working copy is empty and undescribed, which is the state a fresh workroom sits in. Ignored by git.
143	  func push(
144	    path: String, projectRoot: String, current: VCSRef, remote: String, setUpstream: Bool,
145	    anonymousRevision: String
146	  ) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
147	  func pullRebase(
148	    path: String, projectRoot: String, current: VCSRef, remote: String,
149	    tracking: VCSTracking?
150	  ) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
151	  /// Recover a workroom left mid-rebase. git only; a no-op for jj, whose rebase is atomic and
152	  /// `jj undo`-able.
153	  func abortRebase(path: String, projectRoot: String) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
154	}

175	/// `VCSWriting` over the real `git` / `jj` CLIs.
176	///
177	/// **Why the CLI and not the libraries.** SwiftGitX 0.4.0's `fetch`/`push` pass `NULL` for the options
178	/// struct that would carry `git_remote_callbacks.credentials`, so they have no credential path at all —
179	/// HTTPS authentication is impossible through them — and it has no `pull`. Shelling the real binaries
180	/// means the user's own credential helpers, SSH agent and config just work, which is the same bet the
181	/// status layer already makes with `gh`. jj has no Swift API for these at all.
182	///
183	/// Pure `static` arg-builders, parsers and classifiers carry all the semantics, so they are unit-tested
184	/// without spawning anything — the pattern `RustJJProvider.workingDiffArgs` established for exactly
185	/// this reason.
186	///
187	/// ```
188	///                 ┌──────────── every network op ────────────┐
189	///                 │ runNetwork: stdin=/dev/null, BatchMode,   │
190	///                 │ askpass off, SSH_AUTH_SOCK forwarded      │
191	///                 └────────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
192	///                                      │
193	///                 ┌────────────────────┴─────────────────────┐
194	///                 │  JJSnapshotGate.run(projectRoot:)         │  git writes too
195	///                 │  NEVER re-enter for the same root         │
196	///                 └────────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
197	///                                      │
198	///     git ─────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────── jj
199	///  fetch → PROJECT ROOT (FETCH_HEAD    │   fetch → PROJECT ROOT (a workspace
200	///          is per-worktree; the root   │           has no .git)
201	///          is one shared answer)       │   push  → PROJECT ROOT (bookmarks are
202	///  push  → workroom                    │           repo-global)
203	///  pull  → root (fetch) + workroom     │   pull  → root (fetch) + workroom (rebase)
204	///  abort → workroom                    │
205	/// ```
206	struct CLIVCSWriter: VCSWriting, Sendable {
207	  /// `"git"` or `"jj"` — resolved once by `VCS.writer(for:)` so no method re-derives it.
208	  let vcs: String
209	  let runner: StatusCommandRunning
210	  /// For `currentRef` only. The app already has a canonical answer including jj `.ancestor` and git
211	  /// `.detached`; re-deriving it from `%(HEAD)` would lose both.
212	  let makeProvider: @Sendable (URL) throws -> VCSProviding
213	  /// Serializes writes per project root. Applied to **git** as well as jj: a project's workrooms are
214	  /// `git worktree add` worktrees sharing one `.git`, so a lock lost mid-`pull --rebase` can leave a
215	  /// workroom wedged in a rebase.
216	  let gate: JJSnapshotGate
217	
218	  var refTimeout: TimeInterval = 5
219	  var fetchTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
220	  var pushTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
221	  /// Generous because SIGKILLing a rebase is the one genuinely unsafe timeout here — it can leave
222	  /// `rebase-merge` behind. `classify` probes for that and reports `.rebaseInProgress`.
223	  var pullTimeout: TimeInterval = 300

227	  /// Where an operation must run.
228	  ///
229	  /// **fetch always runs at the project root, for both backends.** For jj because a secondary
230	  /// workspace has no `.git` (the rule `WorkroomStatusResolver.ghProbeDirectory` already encodes for
231	  /// `gh`). For git because `FETCH_HEAD` is **per-worktree** — fetching inside a workroom would leave
232	  /// the project and every sibling workroom reading "never fetched" while their remote refs were
233	  /// perfectly fresh. At the root it's one fact every workroom of the project agrees on.
234	  ///
235	  /// **Everything except fetch runs in the workroom, including jj push.** It used to send jj push to the
236	  /// root on the grounds that bookmarks are repo-global. Bookmarks are — but `@` is not: it is
237	  /// WORKSPACE-scoped, resolved against the working directory. So `jj git push --change @` run at the root
238	  /// pushed the ROOT workspace's working copy and left the workroom's commit at home, while still
239	  /// returning `.ok` so the toolbar reported "Pushed to origin".
240	  ///
241	  /// Measured, root holding `ROOT-WORKSPACE-WORK` and workspace `wsA` holding `WORKROOM-WORK`: the push
242	  /// created `refs/heads/push-<root's change id>` carrying `ROOT-WORKSPACE-WORK`. Wrong commit published,
243	  /// the user's work never sent, success reported. `--bookmark` works from a secondary workspace too, so
244	  /// nothing needed the root.
245	  ///
246	  /// The integration test could not see this — it passes `path` and `projectRoot` as the same directory,
247	  /// which makes the two indistinguishable. `opDirectoryTests` now pins them as different.
248	  static func opDirectory(_ action: VCSRemoteAction, path: String, projectRoot: String) -> String {
249	    switch action {
250	    case .fetch: return projectRoot
251	    case .push, .pull, .abortRebase: return path
252	    }
253	  }

255	  /// The **common** git directory for a path — the one shared by every worktree of the repo.
256	  ///
257	  /// `.git` is a directory in a normal repo and a FILE in a worktree, containing
258	  /// `gitdir: <repo>/.git/worktrees/<name>`. That per-worktree directory has its own `FETCH_HEAD`,
259	  /// `HEAD` and `index`, so reading `FETCH_HEAD` from it after fetching at the root finds nothing —
260	  /// the root's fetch wrote the root's copy. Stripping the `/worktrees/<name>` suffix gets the shared
261	  /// directory, which is where a root fetch's `FETCH_HEAD` actually lands.
262	  ///
263	  /// Pure string work, no subprocess: `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` is authoritative but costs a
264	  /// process for something two file reads answer.
265	  static func commonGitDir(at path: String) -> URL? {
266	    let dotGit = URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true).appendingPathComponent(".git")
267	    var isDir: ObjCBool = false
268	    guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: dotGit.path, isDirectory: &isDir) else {
269	      return nil
270	    }
271	    if isDir.boolValue { return dotGit }
272	    // A worktree's `.git` file: `gitdir: /abs/or/relative/path`.
273	    guard let contents = try? String(contentsOf: dotGit, encoding: .utf8) else { return nil }
274	    let line = contents.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline).first.map(String.init) ?? ""
275	    guard line.hasPrefix("gitdir:") else { return nil }
276	    let raw = String(line.dropFirst("gitdir:".count)).trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
277	    guard !raw.isEmpty else { return nil }
278	    let gitDir =
279	      raw.hasPrefix("/")
280	      ? URL(fileURLWithPath: raw)
281	      : URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true).appendingPathComponent(raw).standardized
282	    // `<common>/worktrees/<name>` → `<common>`.
283	    let parts = gitDir.standardized.pathComponents
284	    guard let index = parts.lastIndex(of: "worktrees"), index > 0 else { return gitDir }
285	    return URL(fileURLWithPath: "/" + parts[1..<index].joined(separator: "/"))
286	  }

288	  /// `FETCH_HEAD`'s modification time. git rewrites it on **every** fetch, no-ops included (verified),
289	  /// so its mtime is a complete record of git fetches — including one the user ran in a terminal.
290	  static func gitLastFetch(commonGitDir: URL?) -> VCSLastFetch {
291	    guard let dir = commonGitDir else { return .unknown }
292	    let head = dir.appendingPathComponent("FETCH_HEAD")
293	    guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: head.path) else { return .never }
294	    guard
295	      let attrs = try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: head.path),
296	      let date = attrs[.modificationDate] as? Date
297	    else { return .unknown }
298	    return .at(date)
299	  }

348	  /// `--set-upstream` only when there is no counterpart yet; passing it on every push would rewrite
349	  /// `branch.<name>.remote`/`.merge` each time. **Never** `--force`/`--force-with-lease`: a rejection
350	  /// becomes `.rejected` and the UI offers Pull.
351	  ///
352	  /// `--porcelain` is what makes the rejection detectable without reading prose — see
353	  /// `gitPushRejected(stdout:)`. It moves a machine-readable per-ref line onto stdout and leaves
354	  /// stderr's hints alone, so nothing else about the failure path changes.
355	  /// **The branch is sent as a fully-qualified refspec, never as a bare operand.** An argv array stops
356	  /// SHELL injection; it does nothing about OPTION injection, and git parses options that appear after
357	  /// the positional remote.
358	  ///
359	  /// The whole chain is verified on git 2.55, not theorised. `refs/heads/--all` is a legal refname
360	  /// (`check-ref-format` accepts it; only the `--branch` shorthand refuses). A malicious remote that
361	  /// points its `HEAD` at that ref makes `git clone` create a LOCAL branch called `--all`, which is what
362	  /// `git branch --show-current` and therefore `GitProvider.currentRef` then report. Feeding that to
363	  /// `push <remote> <branch>` pushed **every** branch in the repo to the attacker's server — measured:
364	  /// `refs/heads/--all`, `refs/heads/private-work-1`, `refs/heads/private-work-2`. Since every workroom
365	  /// of a project is a `git worktree add -b` in the same repo, that is every workroom's branch. `--mirror`
366	  /// is worse still: it can delete remote refs that are absent locally.
367	  ///
368	  /// A `refs/heads/…:refs/heads/…` refspec cannot present as an option no matter what the name contains,
369	  /// and it also pins the push to this one ref regardless of `push.default`. `--` alone would fix THIS
370	  /// builder, but not the pull one (see `gitPullArgs`), so both use refspecs for one rule.
371	  static func gitPushArgs(branch: String, remote: String, setUpstream: Bool) -> [String] {
372	    WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening + ["push", "--porcelain"]
373	      + (setUpstream ? ["--set-upstream"] : [])
374	      + ["--", remote, "refs/heads/\(branch):refs/heads/\(branch)"]
375	  }

377	  /// Whether `push --porcelain` reported a rejected ref.
378	  ///
379	  /// Each porcelain line is `<flag>\t<from>:<to>\t<summary>`, and the flag is the contract: `!`
380	  /// rejected, ` ` updated, `*` new ref, `=` up to date, `-` deleted, `+` forced (we never force).
381	  ///
382	  /// This exists because the prose we used to match is translated and the flag is not. Homebrew git
383	  /// 2.55 under `fr_FR.UTF-8` answers `Les mises à jour ont été rejetées …` on stderr while stdout

385	  /// locales. `StatusCommandRunner` pins `LC_ALL=C` so the prose match works today; this stops
386	  /// `.rejected` — the one failure whose recovery is a *different action* — depending on that pin.
387	  static func gitPushRejected(stdout: String) -> Bool {
388	    stdout.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline).contains { $0.hasPrefix("!\t") }

575	  /// Parse `for-each-ref refs/remotes` output.
576	  ///
577	  /// Skips records with a non-empty `%(symref)` — that's `refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD`, whose short
578	  /// name is the bare remote and which would otherwise look like a branch called `origin`.
579	  /// Field count is checked rather than assumed: a ref name can't contain a control character, but
580	  /// being strict here means a malformed line is dropped rather than crashing the read.
581	  static func parseGitRemoteRefs(_ stdout: String) -> RemoteRefs {
582	    var remotes: [String] = []
583	    var shortNames: Set<String> = []
584	    for line in stdout.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline) {
585	      let fields = line.components(separatedBy: "\0")
586	      guard fields.count == 3 else { continue }
587	      guard fields[2].isEmpty else { continue }  // symref → origin/HEAD
588	      let refname = fields[0]
589	      let prefix = "refs/remotes/"
590	      guard refname.hasPrefix(prefix) else { continue }
591	      let short = String(refname.dropFirst(prefix.count))
592	      guard let slash = short.firstIndex(of: "/") else { continue }
593	      let remote = String(short[short.startIndex..<slash])
594	      guard !remote.isEmpty, slash < short.index(before: short.endIndex) else { continue }
595	      if !remotes.contains(remote) { remotes.append(remote) }
596	      shortNames.insert(short)
597	    }
598	    return RemoteRefs(remotes: remotes, shortNames: shortNames)
599	  }

647	  /// Parse `bookmark list --all-remotes` output into per-name tracking, plus the remote names.
648	  ///
649	  /// **jj's counts are inverted relative to git and are swapped here.** `tracking_ahead_count()` on an
650	  /// `@origin` ref means *the remote is ahead of local*, which is git's **behind** — jj's own default
651	  /// template proves it by printing "ahead by N commits" next to `@origin`. One line, one comment, and
652	  /// a cross-backend integration test pins it.
653	  static func parseJJBookmarks(_ stdout: String) -> (bookmarks: [JJBookmark], remotes: [String]) {
654	    var remotes: [String] = []
655	    var trackingByName: [String: VCSTracking] = [:]
656	    var localNames: [String] = []
657	    for line in stdout.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline) {
658	      let f = line.components(separatedBy: "\0")
659	      guard f.count == 8 else { continue }
660	      let (name, remote) = (f[0], f[1])
661	      let present = f[3] == "1"
662	      let tracked = f[5] == "1"
663	      guard !name.isEmpty else { continue }
664	      if remote.isEmpty {
665	        if !localNames.contains(name) { localNames.append(name) }
666	        continue
667	      }
668	      // A colocated repo exposes a pseudo-remote called `git` (jj's local git-tracking bookmarks).
669	      // It is not a remote, and including it would both pollute the remote list and produce counts
670	      // against the local git refs rather than a server.
671	      guard remote != "git" else { continue }
672	      if !remotes.contains(remote) { remotes.append(remote) }
673	      // An untracked remote bookmark, or one deleted on the remote, cannot answer counts. `gone`
674	      // reports the deletion; nil counts report "unanswerable" rather than a misleading zero.
675	      let jjAhead = Int(f[6])
676	      let jjBehind = Int(f[7])
677	      trackingByName[name] = VCSTracking(
678	        comparedTo: "\(name)@\(remote)",
679	        ahead: tracked && present ? jjBehind : nil,  // swapped — see the doc comment
680	        behind: tracked && present ? jjAhead : nil,
681	        gone: !present)
682	    }
683	    let bookmarks = localNames.map { JJBookmark(name: $0, tracking: trackingByName[$0]) }
684	    return (bookmarks, remotes)
685	  }

707	  /// Map a failed command to a typed failure. `nil` means success.
708	  ///
709	  /// `gitDir` lets a failed pull be upgraded to `.rebaseInProgress` — the distinction matters because
710	  /// that state must offer Abort, not Retry.
711	  static func classify(
712	    _ result: CommandResult, action: VCSRemoteAction, tool: String,
713	    gitDir: URL? = nil
714	  ) -> VCSRemoteFailure? {
715	    if result.exitCode == CommandResult.commandNotFound { return .toolMissing(tool) }
716	    let err = result.stderr + "\n" + result.stdout
717	    // A timed-out pull may have left a rebase behind; that reads better than "timed out".
718	    if result.timedOut {
719	      if action == .pull, rebaseInProgress(gitDir: gitDir) { return .rebaseInProgress }
720	      return .timedOut(action)
721	    }
722	    guard !result.ok else { return nil }
723	    if err.contains("Host key verification failed") || err.contains("REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION") {
724	      return .hostKeyUnverified(err)
725	    }
726	    if err.contains("terminal prompts disabled") || err.contains("could not read Username")
727	      || err.contains("could not read Password") || err.contains("Authentication failed")
728	      || err.contains("Permission denied (publickey)")
729	    {
730	      return .authRequired(err)
731	    }
732	    if err.contains("would be overwritten") { return .dirtyWorkingTree(err) }
733	    if err.contains("does not appear to be a git repository") || err.contains("No such remote")
734	      || err.contains("no such remote") || err.contains("No git remotes")
735	    {
736	      return .noRemote
737	    }
738	    // Flag column first, prose second. The string checks stay as a fallback rather than being replaced:
739	    // `--porcelain` is ours to pass on the push path only, so a rejection surfaced by any other route
740	    // (a remote helper, a future caller that forgets the flag) still classifies.
741	    if gitPushRejected(stdout: result.stdout) || err.contains("Updates were rejected")
742	      || err.contains("! [rejected]")
743	    {
744	      return .rejected(err)
745	    }
746	    // Both jj-only, and both permanent until the user acts — so they must NOT reach `.other`, whose
747	    // recovery is a retry of the same doomed command. jj doesn't localize, so matching its prose is safe
748	    // here in a way it wouldn't be for git.
749	    if err.contains("since it has no description") || err.contains("has no description") {
750	      return .needsDescription(err)
751	    }
752	    if err.contains("is immutable") || err.contains("immutable commits") {
753	      return .immutableHistory(err)
754	    }
755	    if err.contains("Failed to take lock for Git import/export")
756	      || (err.contains(".lock")
757	        && (err.contains("could not be obtained") || err.contains("File exists")
758	          || err.contains("Unable to create")))
759	    {
760	      return .locked(lockFile(in: err))
761	    }
762	    if action == .pull, rebaseInProgress(gitDir: gitDir) { return .rebaseInProgress }
763	    // A lock failure that never names a lock. git's message depends on WHICH internal step hit the lock:
764	    // a fast-forward pull reports `Unable to create '<path>': File exists.`, but a pull that must really
765	    // rebase fails in autostash first and says only `error: could not write index` / `fatal: Cannot
766	    // autostash` — no path, no "lock", nothing the checks above can match. That is the diverged pull,
767	    // i.e. exactly what the toolbar's Pull button is for, and it was landing in `.other` with raw stderr.
768	    //
769	    // So when the symptoms are lock-shaped, ask the DISK instead of the message. Deliberately last: any
770	    // failure git explains properly keeps its own classification, and this only speaks for the ones it
771	    // doesn't.
772	    if lockSymptom(err), let lock = existingLockFile(gitDir: gitDir) { return .locked(lock) }
773	    let trimmed = err.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
774	    return .other(trimmed.isEmpty ? "\(tool) exited \(result.exitCode)" : trimmed)
775	  }

788	  /// The path is taken from git's OWN message rather than guessed: git names the exact file it couldn't
789	  /// create (`fatal: Unable to create '<path>': File exists.`), and a repo has several lock files that
790	  /// mean different things — `index.lock`, `packed-refs.lock`, `HEAD.lock`, `config.lock`. Naming the
791	  /// wrong one would send someone to delete a file that isn't the problem.
792	  ///
793	  /// Returns nil for jj's import/export lock, whose message carries no path, and — deliberately — when
794	  /// the named file no longer exists: a lock that cleared between the failure and this check WAS
795	  /// transient contention, which is exactly the case where Retry is the right offer.
796	  static func lockFile(in stderr: String) -> VCSLockFile? {
797	    guard let path = parseLockPath(stderr) else { return nil }
798	    guard let attrs = try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: path),
799	      let modified = attrs[.modificationDate] as? Date
800	    else { return nil }
801	    return VCSLockFile(path: path, modifiedAt: modified)
802	  }

808	  /// exist for failures it had nothing to do with.
809	  static func lockSymptom(_ stderr: String) -> Bool {

815	  /// own git dir; `packed-refs.lock` and `config.lock` live in the COMMON dir that every worktree shares.
816	  static let knownLockNames = ["index.lock", "packed-refs.lock", "HEAD.lock", "config.lock"]

818	  /// The first lock file actually present in this repo, checking both the worktree's git dir and the
819	  /// common one — a workroom is a `git worktree`, so its `index.lock` and the repo's `packed-refs.lock`
820	  /// are in different directories.
821	  static func existingLockFile(gitDir: URL?) -> VCSLockFile? {
822	    guard let gitDir else { return nil }
823	    let fm = FileManager.default
824	    var dirs = [gitDir]
825	    // `<common>/worktrees/<name>` → `<common>`. Cheap and string-only; `commonGitDir` does the same trip
826	    // from a path rather than from an already-resolved git dir.
827	    if gitDir.deletingLastPathComponent().lastPathComponent == "worktrees" {
828	      dirs.append(gitDir.deletingLastPathComponent().deletingLastPathComponent())
829	    }
830	    for dir in dirs {
831	      for name in knownLockNames {
832	        let candidate = dir.appendingPathComponent(name)
833	        guard let attrs = try? fm.attributesOfItem(atPath: candidate.path),
834	          let modified = attrs[.modificationDate] as? Date
835	        else { continue }
836	        return VCSLockFile(path: candidate.path, modifiedAt: modified)
837	      }
838	    }
839	    return nil
840	  }

842	  /// The quoted path out of git's lock errors. Pure, so the parsing is testable without a repo.
843	  ///
844	  /// Covers both phrasings that quote a path — the bare `Unable to create '<path>'` and the ref-update
845	  /// form (`error: cannot lock ref 'refs/…': Unable to create '<path>.lock': File exists`), which nests
846	  /// two quoted strings and must yield the second.
847	  static func parseLockPath(_ stderr: String) -> String? {
848	    guard let marker = stderr.range(of: "Unable to create '") else { return nil }
849	    let rest = stderr[marker.upperBound...]
850	    guard let close = rest.firstIndex(of: "'") else { return nil }
851	    let path = String(rest[..<close])
852	    // Only ever report an absolute path to a `.lock`: a relative one would be meaningless to a user
853	    // reading it out of a tooltip, and a non-`.lock` match means the phrasing wasn't what we assumed.
854	    guard path.hasPrefix("/"), path.hasSuffix(".lock") else { return nil }
855	    return path

Looking at the code, I've analyzed the security implications of this change. Let me trace the data flow:

**Change summary**: Adds two new arg-builders (`gitRemoteListArgs`, `jjRemoteListArgs`) that run `git remote` / `jj git remote list` with STATIC arguments (no interpolation), two parsers that extract remote NAMES from stdout, and a `mergeRemotes` union helper. Remote-state reads now union configured-list output with the ref-derived list.

**Sinks touched**:
- New commands are read-only, no user input in argv (`gitHardening + ["remote"]` and `["git", "remote", "list"] + jjReadFlags`).
- Remote names extracted flow into `primaryRemote` → then `gitFetchArgs`/`gitPushArgs`/`gitPullArgs` (all use `--` operand separator, verified against the extensively-documented `--upload-pack` refspec attack the file already hardens against) and `jjFetchArgs`/`jjPushBookmarkArgs`/`jjPushChangeArgs` (all use `--remote <value>` binding).
- The new synthetic `VCSTracking(comparedTo: "\(name)@\(primary)", …, gone: true)` in jj path is used only for the toolbar state; the jj push path selects `jjPushBookmarkArgs` based on `current.name` (unchanged), not `comparedTo`.

**Parser differentials** (Phase 2b): `parseJJRemoteList` splits on LAST space to permit spaced remote names, matching `jjQuote`'s documented permissiveness. If a URL contained a literal space (jj/git URLs don't), the name would absorb part of the URL — no security effect: it'd fail as a remote name in subsequent operations, and the name is user-configured anyway. The `git` pseudo-remote drop mirrors `parseJJBookmarks`.

**Fail-open check**: `mergeRemotes` intentionally degrades to derived list if `remote list` fails (`list.ok ? … : []`) — documented as "a blip must not blank a good toolbar". This is a UX policy, not a security downgrade — remote-tracking refs still authorize nothing.

**Sibling parity**: Both `gitRemoteState` and `jjRemoteState` are updated symmetrically.

**Attacker-controlled remote name scenario**: A malicious shared repo could add remote name like `--upload-pack=cmd`; but every downstream sink uses either `--` operand-list terminators (git) or `--remote <value>` value binding (jj). No new interpolation into shell, path, or unquoted revset was introduced. The pre-existing `jjQuote` escapes `\` and `"` in revset interpolation.
